subject: mathematics
question_text: If A is the matrix with rows (−2, 1), (5, 0) and (−1, 4), and B is the matrix with rows (−2, 3, 1) and (4, 0, 2), then find 2A + Bᵀ and 3Bᵀ − A.

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), chapter 5 MATRICES, Very Short Answer question 10, book p.33. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+1 split gives one mark to each of the two matrices asked for, and Bᵀ is written inside the first step because both parts need it. ORDERS: A is 3×2 and B is 2×3, so Bᵀ is 3×2 and both sums are defined; A + B itself would not be. CHECKED: every entry of both answers was recomputed a second time straight from the stem, as 2aᵢⱼ + bⱼᵢ and 3bⱼᵢ − aᵢⱼ, and matched. Paper position: Maths-1A Section A runs Q1 to Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory, under the 2026-27 pattern. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would work out 2A + Bᵀ and 3Bᵀ − A here.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write Bᵀ and find 2A + Bᵀ
steps.margin_note: First mark. Check the orders before adding anything: A is 3×2, B is 2×3, so Bᵀ is 3×2 and matches A. A + B on its own is not defined at all.
steps.memory_tip: Row 1 of Bᵀ is column 1 of B. Read B down its columns and write each column as a row.
lines: A is 3×2 and B is 2×3, so Bᵀ is 3×2.

recall.must_convey: That Bᵀ is 3×2 so it can be added to A, and 2A + Bᵀ is found entry by entry.
accept: transpose B first so it is three by two like A then add
B transpose makes the orders match, then double A and add
columns of B become rows of B transpose, then add to two A
B transpose teeskunte three by two avuthundi, appudu add cheyyachu
double every entry of A and add the transpose

steps.why: Matrices add only when they have the same order. Transposing B is what makes the addition possible, so checking the orders is part of the answer, not a preliminary.
common_mistakes: Adding A and B directly, which is not defined.
Writing Bᵀ as a 2×3 matrix by reversing the rows instead of exchanging rows with columns.

steps.label: Find 3Bᵀ − A
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Scale first, subtract second. Note the order of the subtraction: it is 3Bᵀ − A, not A − 3Bᵀ.
steps.memory_tip: Multiply Bᵀ by 3 first, then subtract A once. Subtracting before scaling changes the answer.

lines.text: ∴ 2A + Bᵀ and 3Bᵀ − A are as above

recall.must_convey: That 3Bᵀ is formed first and A is then subtracted from it, giving a 3×2 matrix with rows (−4, 11), (4, 0) and (4, 2).
accept: multiply B transpose by three then subtract A entry by entry
three times B transpose minus A gives minus four eleven, four zero, four two
scale first and subtract second, keeping the order three B transpose minus A
mundu three tho multiply chesi taruvatha A ni subtract cheyyali
the second answer is also a three by two matrix

steps.why: Scalar multiplication reaches every entry, and subtraction acts position by position. Doing the scaling before the subtraction keeps the work to one pass.
common_mistakes: Computing A − 3Bᵀ and getting every sign wrong.
Subtracting A before multiplying Bᵀ by 3.
